subject: Locality commitment scope and conditional failover runbook
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@luminahealth.com>

Subject: Locality commitment request & conditional failover planning

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this on. Lumina Health is moving toward a procurement milestone and we need a clear, written description of Redwood's locality/residency commitments for PHI workloads. Specifically:

- Can Redwood commit to keeping patient-derived inference data (inputs and model-generated output) physically stored and processed within the US commercial region for our production tenant?
- In the event of an outage in the primary region, what is the maximum window Redwood may perform cross-region synchronization (temporary replication) to restore service? We need an upper bound to include in our DPA addendum.
- Please provide the current subprocessor roster, including where each subprocessors' processing is located by region, and any planned additions in the next 90 days.
- We also need a short ops-runbook/escrow procedure describing notification and approval steps Lumina would receive before any temporary cross-border processing occurs.

Attachments: none on this message.

Our timeline: procurement asks for written answers + draft MAP by next Wednesday (7/28). If useful, happy to jump on a 30-minute call.

Cheers,
Elena Rossi
Data Protection Officer

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. I looped in Monica (account lead) and Markus (legal) so we can cover ops + contract details. High-level answers below; we'll follow with a short MAP and attachments by end of week.

1) Residency: Redwood provides region affinity controls that keep data and inference processing within a chosen cloud region (e.g., us-west-2) by default. For Lumina we can scope the production tenant to US-only physical nodes and commit to storing at-rest artifacts in US region media. We will document this in the DPA addendum.

2) Temporary cross-region sync: our standard high-availability failover policy may, in extreme degraded scenarios, perform a bounded cross-region synchronization to restore service. Typical configured maximum windows are customer-definable; default operational practice is to avoid cross-region sync and rely on multi-az within-region recovery. For procurement purposes we can offer a conditional failover window (example: up to 48 hours) as an explicit carve-out in the DPA addendum, with pre-approved notification and an approval workflow. Markus will propose contract language.

3) Subprocessors: Markus will attach the roster and a short table mapping each subprocessors' processing region. We'll include planned activations within 90 days.

4) Ops runbook / approvals: Monica will draft a short mutual action plan that outlines notification cadence, emergency contact roster, and required Lumina approvals before any cross-region replication is initiated. We'll include expected SLAs for notification (e.g., 2-hour initial notice, followed by a written summary).

A couple quick clarifying Qs so we scope the MAP correctly:
- Is the requirement to keep all derived artifacts (embeddings, logs, traces) in-region, or only inference inputs/outputs?
- Do you have a threshold (requests/day or tokens/day) that would trigger our dedicated-capacity offering vs. hosted? That will influence the technical runbook.

We aim to send: redline DPA, subprocessor roster CSV, and a first-pass MAP draft by Fri 7/23. If that timeline doesn't work for procurement, tell us what date you need.

Cheers,

Elena / Naomi — attaching the requested materials for review.

Attachments included (stubs):
- redline_DPA_Lumina.pdf (summary of proposed addendum language)
- subprocessor_roster.csv (current processors + region mapping; planned activations flagged)

Summary of key contract points in the redline:
- We will add an addendum that:
  * Affirms at-rest storage and primary processing will occur in the US region for the scoped production tenant.
  * Defines a "Conditional Failover Window" clause: temporary cross-region synchronization is permitted only under documented emergency conditions and is capped at a mutually-agreed maximum window. We propose 48 hours as the default cap for emergency temporary sync; this remains negotiable.
  * Requires Redwood to provide immediate notification to Lumina's DPO and a written incident report within the notification cadence in the MAP before any cross-region sync where feasible.
- Limitations: cannot provide an absolute guarantee against all cross-border transfers in all disaster scenarios without a technical escrow (e.g., dedicated on-prem or fully isolated hardware + contractual escrow of keys). Where absolute geo-lock is required, we'll recommend Redwood Private or a dedicated capacity arrangement and an engineer-led technical design session.

Please review the attachments; Monica will follow up with the MAP draft and an ops-runbook the team can sign off on. If Lumina wants an extension of the failover window or an alternative SLA (e.g., 24h cap), call that out and we can propose pricing/controls.

Naomi / Markus / Monica — thanks for the quick turnaround and the materials. I reviewed the redline and the roster; the list looks complete for now. A few items and next steps:

1) MAP: please send the Mutual Action Plan as an editable spreadsheet (we prefer Excel). We'll add our DPO acceptance cell and a planned timeline. I attached our internal template for reference in a separate message (ops will share).
2) Failover window: 48 hours is acceptable as an initial agreed cap for the addendum. We will reserve the right to request a shorter cap (24h) for specific sub-tenants after a short pilot.
3) Ops runbook: we need a one-page runbook with the exact notification cadence, named contacts, and the run-level approvals (who on Lumina side must sign off). Ops will validate the cadence against our incident policy.
4) Evidence: please include a statement of where audit logs for the temporary sync events are stored and how long telemetry is retained.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call Tues 7/27 or Wed 7/28 to finalize the MAP and sign the addendum. Here's a scheduling link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=lumina-finalize-geo-commit (ops copied).
